content:
tara: Heads-up — we're seeing intermittent NCCL 2.26 peer disconnects in us-east-2 after the driver 535.101 rollout. A couple of mixed vGPU inference jobs hang during allgather/allreduce. Anyone seen this pattern?

ops-bot: Alert: node-prod-gpu-42 reported `NCCL WARN Peer closed connection` x7 in the last 10m. Pod autoscaler suppressed scale-ups.

sanjay: Yep, I saw similar flips this morning in canary — looks like peer reconfig during VFIO remap is causing a short net dev tear down. Only affects mixed vGPU + multi-GPU container workloads.

leo: Can you paste a short log snippet? Are the hangs symmetric (all ranks) or leader-only?

maria: Also: which kernel version did we push with 535.101? I remember a kernel patch around DMA remap a few weeks back.

tara: Log excerpt: ```
[2026-03-17T21:13:02Z] NCCL WARN Allgather failed, ret = INTERNAL, rank 0->1, peer closed connection
[2026-03-17T21:13:02Z] ncclTransportP2p: connect failed: errno=104 Connection reset by peer
[2026-03-17T21:13:02Z] GPU0: stall waiting for nvlink peer handshake
```

sanjay: That errno=104 matches a socket-level reset during peer init. My hypothesis: vGPU remap triggers device re-enumeration -> kernel rebind -> temporary device offline -> NCCL times out and stalls collective.

leo: Quick checks: `nvidia-smi topo --matrix` before/after remap to see broken topology, and `dmesg | tail` for vfio/iommu messages. Also check `kubectl describe pod` for OOM/eviction events.

maria: Kernel we rolled is 6.6.17-custom (vfio remap patches). If that's the interaction, we can either 1) roll the driver back to 535.63 which doesn't trigger the remap path, or 2) pin vGPU scheduling to single-device jobs until we get a driver/kernel patch.

jason: If we rollback drivers in us-east-2 we'll need to drain ~120 GPU nodes for a rolling update — that blocks ~30% of our reserved capacity during the window. Cost: if we divert workloads to on-demand in us-west-1 for the mitigation window, estimate +$18k/day in extra cloud spend. Need ops approval.

infra-oncall: For immediate mitigation I recommend: A) cordon + drain affected node pools that show repeated NCCL resets, B) disable mixed vGPU placement scheduling (scheduler daemonset patch), C) open hotline with driver vendor to prioritize a patch. I'll own the drains and scheduler change, need a thumbs-up.

tara: Thumbs-up from me. Plan: canary rollback on 3 nodes in us-east-2 tonight 0100 UTC, validate with our perf harness (allreduce microbench), then stagger the rest if green. Sanjay, can you prepare a pinned image with 535.63 and NCCL 2.25? Leo, can you script the log collection hooks for the canary so we capture nvlink/dmesg/strace on the rank that resets?

sanjay: On it — building pinned image now, will push to staging registry.

leo: I'll add a short script to the canary job: `journalctl -k -f | sed -n '1,200p' > /tmp/canary-dmesg.log` plus `nccl-tests/all_reduce --n 1 --gpus 4 > /tmp/nccl-micro.log 2>&1` and upload on completion.

jason: I'll pre-approve up to $50k emergency spend if the rollback doesn't stabilize and we need cross-region spill. Keep me posted with ETA.

infra-oncall: Rolling plan added to runbook: rollback-canary -> 1h perf validation -> escalate or continue. I'll run the first 3 drains at 01:00 UTC. Expected customer-impact window: ~2.5h for canary, up to 8h if full rollback required.

maria: Also file a support ticket with GPU vendor referencing kernel 6.6.17-custom + driver 535.101 + NCCL 2.26. Include topology snapshots.

tara: Thanks all — please comment inline on the runbook doc I just linked. I'll post updates here after the canary.
